# CLO-to-lecture mapping

## Outcome statements

| CLO | Statement | Assessed by |
|-----|-----------|-------------|
| CLO1 | Given a PMBOK 7 performance-domain map, define and correctly classify the twelve principles, the eight performance domains, and predictive, adaptive, and hybrid life-cycle models; given a project vignette, justify a life-cycle choice using at least three explicit criteria (requirements volatility, regulatory exposure, feedback cadence, team distribution). | Midterm, quizzes |
| CLO2 | Given a project brief, construct a deliverable-oriented WBS that passes the 100% rule, derive three-point (PERT) estimates for its work packages, build a CPM network with correctly computed float, and produce a levelled, time-feasible Gantt baseline within a fixed window. | Assignment 1, Labs 1-4, Midterm |
| CLO3 | Given activity cost data, develop a bottom-up budget with S-curve and a quality/data-quality plan containing at least four measurable metrics and eight enforceable data-quality rules; given PV, EV, and AC, compute the full earned-value set (CV, SV, CPI, SPI, EAC variants, TCPI) correctly. | Midterm (primary); practiced via CS-17, CS-26, CS-57, CS-62 and capstone budget |
| CLO4 | Given a project scenario, identify at least eighteen distinct risks as normalized cause-risk-effect statements, quantify at least one risk via EMV or Monte Carlo simulation, and propose responses with named owners, triggers, and residual risk; given PV/EV/AC data, diagnose project health and recommend a justified recovery action. | Assignment 3, Labs 7-8, Midterm, Capstone checkpoint |
| CLO5 | Given a delivery context, operate Scrum, Kanban, and hybrid flow systems: produce a sprint plan with a single-sentence goal and capacity check, set WIP limits justified by flow metrics, rewrite a feature-first backlog into a hypothesis-driven one for a data/ML project, and prepare a working agreement plus a BATNA-based negotiation plan for a sponsor conflict. | Assignment 4, Labs 9-12, Case portfolio, Capstone |
| CLO6 | Given a project brief, design a complete, internally consistent project management plan (scope, schedule, and cost baselines plus risk, communication, quality, and data-governance plans), then defend its trade-offs — tailoring cuts, risk investments, ethics and AI-use positions — in a rubric-scored oral defense with follow-up questions. | Capstone, Final exam, Case portfolio |

## Reading the matrix

- A bold cell means the CLO is **primarily taught and practiced** in that lecture.
- Bloom level is taken as the highest level targeted across those lectures.
